elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to each Party’s total aggregate liability.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 limits “each Party's total aggregate liability” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The fee-based cap limb consists of fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses “the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the twelve-month fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly sets the cap at the greater of the fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Each Party is excluded from liability for indirect damages.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 provides that neither Party is liable for indirect damages, subject to Excluded Claims and legal excludability.

elements.element: Each Party is excluded from liability for consequential damages.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 provides that neither Party is liable for consequential damages, subject to Excluded Claims and legal excludability.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes either Party’s breach of confidentiality obligations within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data-protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes either Party’s breach of data-protection obligations within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes either Party’s breach of security obligations within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes either Party’s indemnification obligations within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes gross negligence within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes wilful misconduct within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes fraud within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other Party’s intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes infringement or misappropriation of the other Party’s intellectual property within Excluded Claims, which Section 21.1 excludes from the cap.

elements.element: Customer’s payment obligations are not damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 states that Customer’s payment obligations under the Agreement and any Order Form are not damages subject to the cap.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to each Party’s total aggregate liability.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 limits each Party’s total aggregate liability and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The liability cap equals twelve months’ fees.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 does not set the cap solely at twelve months’ fees; it sets the cap at the greater of twelve months’ fees and USD 1,000,000. When twelve months’ fees are below USD 1,000,000, the operative cap is not twelve months’ fees.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3 and therefore excluded from the cap under Section 21.1.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3 and therefore excluded from the cap under Section 21.1.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3 and therefore excluded from the cap under Section 21.1.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3 and therefore excluded from the cap under Section 21.1.

result.reason: The rendered clause fully implements the preferred position: a mutual greater-of cap, mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion, all required uncapped carve-outs, and an express treatment of Customer payment obligations as outside damages subject to the cap. The changes are confined to the cap basis and payment-obligation language needed to reach that position. Assessed independently and literally, the fallback is not fully satisfied because its cap is stated as twelve months’ fees, whereas the rendered clause applies a USD 1,000,000 floor. Drafting is clear overall, although using lowercase “fees” alongside a narrowly defined capitalized “Fees” may invite avoidable interpretive debate.
